concepts.def: The coming of the Holy Spirit on the disciples in Acts 2, when Peter preached and about three thousand people were baptised - the birth of the Church.
Acts describes the community devoted to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer, sharing possessions with those in need.
The young Church faced arrests and violence; Stephen became the first martyr, and persecution scattered believers, who spread the message as they went.
Saul the persecutor was converted on the Damascus road and, as Paul, carried the gospel across the eastern Mediterranean on missionary journeys.
Peter's vision and the baptism of the Roman centurion Cornelius in Acts 10 opened the Church to non-Jews.
The leaders' decision in Acts 15 that Gentile converts need not be circumcised, allowing Christianity to become a faith for all peoples.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christianity: The Early Church — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Christianity: The Early Church brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Christianity: The Early Church.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: On which festival day did the Holy Spirit come upon the disciples in Acts 2?
options: Pentecost
Passover
Tabernacles
Hanukkah

mcqs.q: Whose vision led to the baptism of the Gentile centurion Cornelius?
options: Peter's
Paul's
Stephen's
Barnabas's

mcqs.q: Who became known as the apostle to the Gentiles after his conversion on the Damascus road?
options: Paul
Peter
John
Matthias

mcqs.q: How does Acts describe the life of the first believers?
options: They shared possessions and met for teaching, breaking of bread and prayer
They lived as hermits in the desert
They built great cathedrals
They kept their faith entirely secret

mcqs.q: Did persecution destroy the early Church?
options: The early Church was never persecuted by anyone.
The first Christians were Roman officials.
Persecution nearly wiped out Christianity in its first years.
No - Acts 8 records that scattered believers preached wherever they went, so persecution actually helped spread the message beyond Jerusalem.

mcqs.q: Were the first Christians a completely separate religion from Judaism at the start?
options: Paul was the brother of Jesus.
The first Christians were Roman officials.
Christianity began as an entirely separate religion on the day of Pentecost.
No - the first believers were Jews who worshipped in the Temple and synagogues; separation from Judaism happened gradually as Gentiles joined.

mcqs.q: Was Paul one of the twelve apostles who followed Jesus in Galilee?
options: Paul was one of the original twelve disciples.
No - Paul never followed the earthly Jesus; he claimed apostleship through his encounter with the risen Christ, while Matthias had replaced Judas among the Twelve.
Paul was the brother of Jesus.
The early Church was never persecuted by anyone.
